ambiguities.clause: It cannot know the future and never predicts.
ambiguities.reading_a: The derelict reacts to a person's present motion using habit-knowledge (habits are listed as knowable), so a door opening a half-step ahead of arrival is response, not foreknowledge.
ambiguities.reading_b: The corridor is new to Abe, so opening doors 'one compartment at a time, before he reaches them' requires knowing which door he will walk to next: a forecast of a future event, which the clause forbids.
ambiguities.arbitration: UPHELD — both readings are defensible from the sentence, and bible/timeline.md (Chapter 2 row: 'Doors open ahead of whoever is walking') already commits canon to reading a, so the rule must say so.
ambiguities.applied: R1 amended by worldbuilder (2026-09-23T02:35Z): 'It may act on a habit it has seen (open the door a person always takes next, set a mug where they always set it) but never on anything not yet done or said, and it never predicts an event.' Beat 2.2 unchanged.

ambiguities.clause: It has no voice and makes no sound of its own.
ambiguities.reading_a: Bars only voice-like or deliberate signalling sound; incidental mechanical noise of the door actuators and lights the Means section grants it is not 'a sound of its own'.
ambiguities.reading_b: An absolute: no audible output whatsoever, so an actuator heard opening a hatch breaks the rule.
ambiguities.arbitration: UPHELD — the Means section grants door actuators and cabin lights, and a rule that forbids the sound of a thing it grants is a rule two critics would read against each other.
ambiguities.applied: R2 amended by worldbuilder (2026-09-23T02:35Z): 'It has no voice and makes no sound beyond the ordinary working of the doors and lights it already controls.' Beat 2.2 unchanged.

ambiguities.clause: The derelict knows only what the crew has already done or said aboard it or on the tug — names, habits, old arguments, private griefs.
ambiguities.reading_a: Text in the fourth hand is verbatim retrieval of words Corey Dunn said or wrote aboard the tug while alive, rendered in his known hand.
ambiguities.reading_b: The fourth-hand entries read as new composition in Corey's style, which 'already done or said' does not license.
ambiguities.arbitration: UPHELD — the outline does not say what the fourth hand's entries contain, and a writer left to decide would compose. bible/characters.md already says any writing in that hand is canon-Corey; the rule now fixes what that may contain.
ambiguities.applied: R1 amended by worldbuilder (2026-09-23T02:35Z): 'Text in a crew member's hand reproduces only words that person actually said or wrote aboard either ship; it composes nothing new in anyone's voice.' Beat 2.1 unchanged; the chapter 2 writer's packet carries the amended rule.
